card_quote: I like things that can be played out loud with friends, and I'm the team's specialist in science and 'weird facts'.
how_read: Dipped in. Read How to play, ran Round 1 out loud with my roommate voting by hand, then jumped straight to Round 6 because physics is my round on the team, then went back and did bits of Rounds 3 and 4. Not cover to cover. By the end of the week I'd got as far as the end of Round 6 and haven't touched the rest.

w1_best.why: The wing explanation I got taught at school is wrong and NASA says so. Everyone at my trivia table has this one wrong.
The cat was an objection, not a claim. Great correction to say out loud.
Trumpeters on a train. Perfect for a table: sounds invented and isn't.
Bones healing stronger is something my gym friends all swear to.
Einstein's Nobel not being for relativity. Clean question, clean answer.

w1_flat.why: No single answer, roots against words. Dead for a team vote.
A technicality about slits versus pinholes.
Disputed, goes round in circles about who said it.
Fourier transforms. My eyes slid off.
Newton apple twice with opposite answers, felt like a gotcha.

w1_review.headline: Great for trivia night, drier than I hoped
w1_review.body: The guess-then-turn format is exactly what my team needs and the physics round is the best part. It loses points for too many DISPUTED answers you can't really vote on and for answer pages that run long when you're trying to read them out loud. A couple of pages looked off too, one where the verdict said TRUE but the text said the opposite. Bottom line: I'd recommend it to my trivia team, and I'd buy it for a friend with a rent budget only if it's cheap.

w2_review_first: It's a fun format for trivia night, the physics round especially. A few answers are a bit dry and some of them can't be scored because they come out as disputed.

w2_lost.why: Snow words, three different counts and I still had no answer.
The uncertainty principle page is correct but heavy.
Young and slits, I didn't care about the pinhole detail.
Long statistics explanation for something I thought I knew.

w2_read_aloud.why: Everyone has a theory about which way their sink drains, instant argument.
Half the table will say yes.
NASA debunks it, and there's a good chance someone at the table teaches it.
The train and the trumpeters is a picture people can see.

w2_cut.why: No clean answer for the team vote.
Mechanism names and hertz numbers, too much for the table.
Can't score it because it's disputed, even though I like the story.

w2_book2: If it's the same format with more disputed answers I can't score, or if it needs one person reading the dense answer page to everyone.
